families.family: linear + bias + fused activation forward
families.reference: act(F.linear(x, W, b)) with act per constexpr ACTIVATION: ''->identity, 'tanh'->torch.tanh, 'gelu'->F.gelu(approximate='none'), 'fast_gelu'->F.gelu(approximate='tanh'), 'relu'->F.relu; optional act_inputs = F.linear(x, W, b)
families.notes: Inference only (no backward). x 2D or 3D (flatten(0,1)); W [N,K] torch layout; fp32 accumulation; inputs cast to fp16 under autocast (custom_fwd cast_inputs=fp16). M/N tails handled by modulo wrap + store mask; act_inputs store unmasked but writes duplicate identical values. Whole library targets triton==2.0.0 (tl.libdevice, triton.ops.matmul_perf_model) - must be ported for Triton 3.x. README benchmarks were run on RTX 3090 (sm_86).

families.family: batched matmul
families.notes: BUG: K mask uses k_range_offs < K (not k + k_range_offs), so K tail is never masked; K must be a multiple of BLOCK_K (32) (assert commented out). Accumulator always cast to fp16 before store, so fp32 inputs get fp16-rounded results. Not wired into the optimizer.

families.family: layer_norm forward, single-pass Welford (IS_RMSNORM=False)
families.reference: F.layer_norm(x, (N,), weight, bias, eps_eff) with eps_eff = max(eps, 1.6e-5) if x.dtype==fp16 else eps; also writes mean and rstd (fp32, biased var)
families.notes: Code-visible deviation: eps silently raised to 1.6e-5 for fp16 inputs. Chan/Welford block merge verified correct. Weight required. Inputs cast to fp16 under autocast; optimizer also converts LayerNorm weights to fp16 in place. Inference only (no backward despite save_for_backward).

families.family: rms_norm forward via the layer-norm kernel (IS_RMSNORM=True)
families.reference: F.rms_norm(x, (N,), weight, eps_eff) (+ bias if HAS_BIAS); eps_eff as in layer_norm family
families.notes: Optimizer replaces the T5-style pattern (eps=1e-6) with this kernel; for fp16 the kernel raises eps to 1.6e-5, deviating from the replaced pattern. Stored mean is 0.

families.family: layer_norm forward benchmark-only variants (xformers single block, tutorial multi-pass)
families.notes: Docstrings: 'only used in benchmarks'. Both ignore HAS_BIAS/IS_RMSNORM and always load bias; with bias=None the wrapper passes the input tensor as bias pointer, so garbage is added. xformers variant needs N <= 4096 (single block).

families.family: flash attention forward (additive mask / causal)
families.reference: attention_reference in the same file: softmax(q@k^T*sm_scale + mask' [+ top-left causal -inf], -1) @ v, where kernel uses mask' = mask.masked_fill(mask == -inf, torch.finfo(mask.dtype).min)
families.notes: fp16/bf16 only (fp32 cast to fp16 by custom_fwd). Mask additive, broadcastable over batch/heads/rows; -inf replaced by dtype min (fully masked row -> mean of v instead of NaN; library reference gives NaN). Causal is top-left aligned. Fixed BLOCK 128, no autotune. BUG: N-padding mask uses n_range_offs < n_size instead of block_n_offs, so for n_size > 128 with n_size % 128 != 0, no mask and non-causal, padded keys (k=0) enter the softmax denominator -> output scaled down (hidden in tests because q,k = rand >= 0 make real scores dominate).

families.family: skinny attention part 1: split-KV partial blocks
families.reference: attention_split_1_reference in the same file: per 128-key block j: blocks_j = exp(S_j - max_j) @ V_j (unnormalized, stored fp16), maximums_j = rowmax(S_j), sums_j = rowsum(exp(S_j - max_j)), S = q@k^T*sm_scale (+mask, +causal)
families.notes: Wired by optimizer only for q_len==1, k_len>50, no mask, non-causal. Intermediate layout [B,H,cdiv(N,128),M,D] fp16 + fp32 max/sum [B,H,n_div,M]. Same padded-key bug as flash attention (affects the wired path whenever k_len > 128 and k_len % 128 != 0). Fully masked block (causal) gives NaN (exp(-inf - -inf)). Library reference only valid when N divisible by n_div.

families.family: skinny attention part 2: merge of split-KV partials
families.reference: L = maximums.max(2, keepdim); w = exp(maximums - L); out = (w[...,None] * blocks).sum(2) / (w * sums).sum(2)[...,None]
families.notes: Online merge over n_div partials; NaN partials from part 1 propagate.

families.family: vec-mat (single-query attention building block)
families.reference: s = vec.float() * scaler; s = torch.softmax(s, -1) if softmax_vec else s; s @ (matrix.transpose(-1,-2) if transpose_mat else matrix).float()  (vec [B,H,1,K])
families.notes: Used by attention_vec_mat_forward (q@k^T then softmax(sm_scale*s)@v; no mask/causal); not wired into the optimizer, only tests. BUG: with softmax, padded lanes (K not pow2) are loaded as 0 and included in max/sum -> denominator inflated. scaler is a float constexpr (recompile per value).
